scams.name: Zona Colonial Motorcycle Phone-Snatch Drive-By
scams.tldr: She was standing still on a Zona Colonial corner near Parque Colón, head down, iPhone in both hands, checking directions to the Catedral Primada de América.
scams.description: She was standing still on a Zona Colonial corner near Parque Colón, head down, iPhone in both hands, checking directions to the Catedral Primada de América. A motorcycle with two riders had rolled past slowly on a previous lap; she didn't notice.
scams.avoidance: Never use your phone while standing on a street corner or near the curb. Step inside a shop or restaurant to check your phone or maps. Walk on the side of the sidewalk farthest from the road. Keep your phone in a deep front pocket when not in use. Use a phone lanyard or wrist strap so it can't be easily yanked away.
scams.location: Zona Colonial streets (Calle El Conde, Calle Las Damas, Parque Colón), Malecón Avenida George Washington, Parque Independencia, Avenida Mella

scams.name: Calle El Conde Cocaine-Handshake Police-Setup Shakedown
scams.tldr: Walking back from dinner along Calle El Conde at 10 PM, the tourist was greeted by a chipper local — "amigo, where you from?
scams.description: Walking back from dinner along Calle El Conde at 10 PM, the tourist was greeted by a chipper local — "amigo, where you from? New York? My cousin lives there!" Big smile, big handshake, compliments on the shoes. The local seemed friendly enough that he relaxed.
scams.avoidance: Avoid handshakes from strangers on the street, especially at night. If something is placed in your hand, drop it immediately and walk away. Never pay a 'fine' on the street — insist on going to a police station. Keep your hands in your pockets when approached by overly friendly strangers. Travel in groups at night in the Zona Colonial.
scams.location: Calle El Conde, Plaza España, Zona Colonial bar zone, Malecón nightlife strip near Avenida George Washington

scams.name: Alcázar de Colón Camera-Drop Blame-Game Extortion
scams.tldr: Standing in the courtyard of the Alcázar de Colón, a group of three young men approached, smiling: "amigo, una foto, please?" They handed him an older Android phone with an already-cracked screen — a tell he missed at the time.
scams.description: Standing in the courtyard of the Alcázar de Colón, a group of three young men approached, smiling: "amigo, una foto, please?" They handed him an older Android phone with an already-cracked screen — a tell he missed at the time.
scams.avoidance: Politely decline when strangers ask you to take their photo. If you do agree, hold the device firmly with both hands over a soft surface. Walk away if they claim you broke something — you owe nothing. Don't engage in negotiations over 'damages' — it emboldens them. If they become aggressive, head toward other tourists or a busy street.
scams.location: Alcázar de Colón, Plaza España, Catedral Primada de América, Parque Colón monuments — Zona Colonial tourist sites

scams.name: Autopista Duarte AMET Cash-Fine Roadside Shakedown
scams.tldr: She had picked up a rental at Las Américas Airport and was driving the Autopista Duarte to the Zona Colonial.
scams.description: She had picked up a rental at Las Américas Airport and was driving the Autopista Duarte to the Zona Colonial. Rental plates are immediately recognizable to Dominican AMET officers. Within 20 minutes, she was waved to the shoulder by an officer in a fluorescent vest.
scams.avoidance: If stopped, politely ask for a written ticket (multa) — real officers issue them. Never pay cash on the spot to police without a receipt. Know that real fines in the DR are paid at a bank or government office, not roadside. Avoid renting a car in Santo Domingo — use Uber or established taxis instead. If pressured, ask for the officer's name and badge number and say you'll go to the station.
scams.location: Avenida George Washington (Malecón), Autopista Duarte exits, Avenida Independencia, perimeter highways near Las Américas Airport

scams.name: Las Américas Airport Flat-Rate Taxi-Stand Gouge
scams.tldr: First-time DR visitors arrived at Las Américas at 7 PM.
scams.description: First-time DR visitors arrived at Las Américas at 7 PM. The airport taxi stand sits directly outside arrivals, and drivers have a near-monopoly because there is no public bus and Uber pickup zones are restricted at SDQ.
scams.avoidance: Use Uber, InDriver, or DiDi instead of street taxis — they have fixed app pricing. Pre-book airport transfers through your hotel for a known rate. Ask your hotel what the fair taxi rate is before you need one. If taking a taxi, agree on the price before getting in and have it in writing. Airport-to-Zona Colonial should be $25-35 USD — don't pay more.
scams.location: Las Américas International Airport (SDQ) arrivals taxi stands, Zona Colonial taxi kiosks, Malecón hotel taxi ranks

scams.name: Mercado Modelo Gringo-Pricing Verbal-Quote Hustle
scams.tldr: Walking the rows at Mercado Modelo, the tourist asked the price of a hand-carved Taino mask.
scams.description: Walking the rows at Mercado Modelo, the tourist asked the price of a hand-carved Taino mask. The vendor sized her up — clothes, accent, sunscreen-pale skin — before naming a number.
scams.avoidance: Always negotiate — the first price is never the real price at markets. Ask a local friend or your hotel what items should cost. Shop where prices are posted and fixed. Learn a few Spanish phrases — vendors charge less when you speak some Spanish. Walk away if the price doesn't drop — vendors often call you back with a better offer.
scams.location: Mercado Modelo, Zona Colonial souvenir shops along Calle El Conde, colmados and small tiendas near Plaza España

scams.name: Santo Domingo Uber Cancel-and-Cash Fare Manipulation
scams.tldr: Friday night, requesting an Uber from a Zona Colonial restaurant to her hotel in Naco — a 12-minute trip on the app for around $4.
scams.description: Friday night, requesting an Uber from a Zona Colonial restaurant to her hotel in Naco — a 12-minute trip on the app for around $4. The driver pulled up, confirmed her name, and locked the doors before she could buckle.
scams.avoidance: Never cancel an Uber ride at the driver's request — pay through the app only. Follow the route on your phone and speak up if the driver deviates. Rate dishonest drivers poorly and report them through the app. Check your Uber account for unexpected charges after any Santo Domingo trip. Consider using InDriver as an alternative — you set the price upfront.
scams.location: Citywide Santo Domingo — especially Las Américas Airport pickups, Zona Colonial bar exits, and Naco/Piantini nightlife
